claims.statement: agent-harness uses a hybrid architecture: an external host-neutral Go core with thin per-host plugin/adapter configuration; host plugins and hooks are install UX and command wrappers only, never core logic, because a Codex-plugin-only or Claude-hook-only core cannot be shared across hosts.

The core is written in Go: single-binary distribution, fast compilation, and CLI/daemon implementation productivity were chosen over Rust's stricter safety for a personal harness, with Rust to be revisited only for future untrusted-code sandboxing or performance-critical components.

Omo native is the third first-party host adapter: install/update/dry-run output, adapter contract goldens, and native-integration verification cover Codex, Claude Code, and Omo in one deterministic order; the harness neither installs Omo itself nor makes it a readiness gate, and Omo's IssueOps mutations bind to PI_SESSION_ID plus a live process receipt — the persistent senpi runtime receipt is accepted as the Omo process identity only for host=omo, so a session ID alone never authorizes a lease.

The core exposes four implemented execution surfaces: CLI one-shot (minimal cross-host surface), `agent-harness mcp` stdio proxy (starts and proxies to the daemon over a Unix socket), `agent-harness daemon` (user-level shared MCP backend with stale lock/pid/socket and stop/status handling), and `agent-harness worker` (lifecycle job records plus a policy-gated read-only run); the daemon is only the MCP proxy backend, not a long-resident job daemon.

CLI dispatch is layered: cmd/harness/main.go delegates to harnessapp.RunRootCommand, which wires dependencies once and routes os.Args through rootcmd.Command (which owns help/version and exit codes, e.g. policy denial exits 3); the canonical command vocabulary and usage text are owned by internal/domain/cli so usage and contract checks cannot drift from routing.

The public contract is 29 top-level CLI commands and 51 advertised MCP tools, with the CLI usage text and MCP tool/resource catalogs pinned by golden files (usage.golden.txt, mcp_tools.golden.json, mcp_resources.golden.json) that fail on drift.

`agent-harness mcp` by default ensures the daemon is running, dials its Unix socket, and pumps newline-delimited JSON-RPC frames between stdio and the socket (bounded reconnect attempts with capped backoff, 4 MiB max frame); setting HARNESS_MCP_DIRECT=1 instead serves MCP directly over stdio without a daemon.

The MCP proxy tracks in-flight request IDs; when the daemon generation changes mid-flight, pending requests (including batch members) are answered with JSON-RPC error -32002 daemon_generation_changed carrying outcome=unknown, automatic_retry=false, and reconcile_required=true, so interrupted operations are never silently retried or reported as succeeded.

The daemon writes an instance record (PID, process start time, executable path, random nonce, executable SHA-256, protocol version, daemon generation) before serving; `daemon status` verifies liveness via a NUL-prefixed private identity probe that cannot collide with valid JSON-RPC traffic, and the daemon distinguishes probe bytes from MCP frames on the same connection before replaying them to the MCP server.

The daemon caps concurrent MCP connections with a slot-channel admission pool (default 256, HARNESS_DAEMON_MAX_CONNECTIONS up to 4096): over-limit connections receive typed error -32001 daemon_connection_limit_reached, while one reserved overflow slot lets a status/classifier client still be answered when the pool is full; the proxy refuses to connect when the daemon reports it is not accepting.

Each daemon connection is wrapped so every Read refreshes the read deadline (idleConn): idle MCP connections are closed after HARNESS_MCP_IDLE_TIMEOUT (default 30 minutes), releasing the admission slot instead of blocking forever on an abandoned client.

Daemon composition builds the MCP dependency set once before the listener starts and hands an immutable snapshot to each stream; the connection accept path never rewrites process-global dependencies, so concurrent sessions read the same contract snapshot and wiring changes take effect only in a new daemon process.
The daemon server removes stale socket/lock files, chmods the Unix socket to 0600, and on shutdown waits up to 30 seconds for active connections before exiting, logging the drain outcome.

The worker records lifecycle job state (enqueue/status/list/cancel/cleanup-stuck) in the `worker` bucket and runs only policy-gated read-only commands: `worker run --read-only` and the MCP tool worker_run_read_only force write/network/shell off before policy evaluation, enqueue records payload redaction and a no-shell safety notice, and per-job locks serialize enqueue/run/cancel state transitions; it is not a general writable shell runner.

The architecture fixes five boundary commitments: (1) core behavior belongs in Go, not a host plugin or hook; (2) CLI JSON, MCP responses, and daemon responses keep identical meaning; (3) host adapters cannot bypass authentication, command policy, or workspace boundaries; (4) hooks provide only SessionStart project-doc context and never block tool calls, create issues/PRs, edit files, or run tests; (5) the worker manages lifecycle jobs and policy-gated read-only evidence commands only.

cmd/harness/harnessapp is the only composition root: it injects concrete adapter implementations into leaf CLI/MCP/daemon/hook packages via an explicit wireDependencies() call (sync.Once, not init() side effects) so wiring is ordered and import-order independent, and it decides which host installers and readback verifiers are assembled.

The core is layered hexagonally with enforced directions: internal/contract owns versioned DTOs shared by CLI/MCP/state (no judgment logic or I/O); internal/domain owns pure rules/reducers/classifiers with filesystem, process, and DB I/O forbidden; internal/application composes contract/domain/port into capability use cases; internal/port holds capability interfaces that depend only on contract vocabulary; internal/adapter/* implements concrete boundaries and is imported by the composition root only.

internal/architecture enforces the layering as a test-only ratchet over the production import graph: forbidden directions fail immediately with no baseline, legacy adapter edges outside the composition root must number zero, the edge inventory must load byte-stably, and state/SQL/network implementation imports must stay in outbound adapters.

Host installation is one host-neutral engine, install.InstallNative, which validates shared inputs, resolves the skill list once, and delegates concrete writes to port.HostInstaller implementations; the composition root passes exactly the three first-party installers (codex, claude, omo), so adding a host means a new HostInstaller plus wiring, not duplicated domain/application policy.

Each host adapter writes only its own user-level surfaces: Codex gets ~/.codex/skills symlinks, ~/.codex/config.toml MCP registration, and ~/.codex/hooks.json SessionStart hook; Claude Code gets ~/.claude/skills symlinks, user-scope MCP, and ~/.claude/settings.json SessionStart hook; Omo gets ~/.omo/agent/skills symlinks, ~/.omo/mcp.json, and ~/.omo/extensions/agent-harness.js mapping session_start and accepted session_compact to the shared hook commands.

Default install/update writes no files into a target repository; repo-local artifacts (.claude/skills/*, .mcp.json, .omo/skills/*, .omo/mcp.json) are created only with explicit --project-local opt-in.

Native activation commits only after strict semantic readback: each host adapter returns per-surface evidence with semantic and raw SHA-256, mode, size, device, and inode, and the composition-root readback verifier requires all three hosts' surfaces plus the exact single-tool IssueOps MCP catalog before evidence is sealed.

Skills are a single host-neutral source tree: one skills/ directory is symlinked into every first-party host (never copied per host), and a fixed 12-name pioneer catalog is enforced in internal/domain/pioneerskill so catalog coverage is verifiable.

All durable state lives under one user state root (~/.local/state/agent-harness/, overridable with HARNESS_STATE_DIR): each capability store directory owns a harness.db holding records as (bucket, id, JSON) rows plus a harness.lock.db used only for cross-process lock spans; project lifecycle state is isolated under projects/<repo-id>/, loop state in loop/harness.db's loop bucket, and IssueOps v1 state in issueops_v1/harness.db's issueops_v1 bucket.

Every read-modify-write span holds a BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction on the lock database for its duration: the write lock dies with the holding process so a crashed holder cannot deadlock later writers, nested spans on the same root are rejected, and no Git/provider/process call runs while an IssueOps cycle lock is held.

IssueOps v1 records are current-only and fail-closed: the reader accepts exactly schema_version=1 in the issueops_v1 bucket, rejects missing/zero/future schema versions and legacy write-authority keys (execution_handoff, execution_workspace, ownership, remote_create_claim) with a generic `invalid state`, ignores the retired bucket entirely, and provides no conversion, promotion, or reset command.

IssueOps v1 is the single execution authority: one record holds exactly one Execution, one canonical worktree, and one active generation; the trust boundary is the exact native actor (host, session/agent ID, process PID/start/executable receipt, canonical cwd, lifecycle ID, generation), while branch names, source cwd, generic session bindings, terminal handles, and stable diffs are not write authority, and hooks are default-deny guards rather than schedulers or lease grantors.

Default installs register only SessionStart context hooks (Codex re-runs SessionStart with source compact after compaction, so SessionStart alone carries the catalog; Omo's extension additionally maps accepted session_compact to the post-compact hook), and the hook CLI renders only the static project-doc catalog: it never touches durable harness state, telemetry, or IssueOps authority, and HARNESS_DISABLE_HOOKS=1 turns hook invocations into no-ops.

The MCP tool catalog has a single ordered source of truth (catalogSections in internal/domain/mcp): both the advertised tools/list and the name-to-dispatch-group routing derive from it, so adding a tool in one catalog function makes it simultaneously advertised (in golden-pinned order) and routable.

Contract stability is mechanically enforced: golden tests pin the CLI usage text, MCP tool/resource catalogs, and a full CLI+MCP response-contract snapshot with environment normalization, and `agent-harness contract schema|check` exposes the same compatibility surface (command list, MCP tool names, required response fields) from the running binary.

Command execution is the most dangerous capability and is policy-gated: an adapter catalog table is the allow/deny source of truth exposed via harness://command-policy, `policy check|fake-run|run --read-only|audit` cover evaluation, fake execution (no command runs), read-only execution (write/network/shell forced off; shell interpreters never allowed), and append-only redacted JSONL audit, with deny defaults for out-of-workspace cwd/paths, unexplained shell interpreters, and secret-like arguments.

Key environment knobs: HARNESS_STATE_DIR overrides the state root, HARNESS_DAEMON_DIR (else <state>/daemon, else ~/.local/state/agent-harness/daemon) overrides the daemon directory, HARNESS_DAEMON_MAX_CONNECTIONS caps MCP admission, HARNESS_MCP_IDLE_TIMEOUT sets the idle-connection deadline, HARNESS_MCP_DIRECT=1 bypasses the daemon, and HARNESS_DISABLE_HOOKS=1 disables lifecycle hooks.

Operational surface: `doctor` is the single cross-system health command (install, state, hooks, MCP, daemon, and project docs together); `state maintain` performs WAL checkpoint truncation and sidecar permission restoration for fixed store roots and projects/<repo-id>; `state prune` is dry-run by default and requires --confirm to delete; the worker exposes enqueue, read-only run, status, list, cleanup-stuck, and cancel; and `mcp cleanup` removes stale proxy processes in dry-run or apply mode.

The MCP catalog deliberately routes a few tools without advertising them: self_augment_history, self_augment_compare, and self_augment_promote alias the self_verify_history/compare/promote tools under self-augment-prefixed state keys, and their catalogSections entry is marked advertised=false so tools/list stays free of duplicate-looking names while DispatchMap still routes them.

The shared skills/ tree is the single source of truth for 33 skills: the 12 fixed pioneer names enforced by internal/domain/pioneerskill plus 21 operational host/workflow/docs/QA skills, with counts verified via agent-harness inspect --json and each skills/<name>/SKILL.md.

A test golden locks the three-host install contract: TestNativeInstallAdapterContractMatrix snapshots InstallNative behavior for user-global-default and project-local-opt-in cases into native_install_contract_matrix.golden.json, so host-adapter surface drift fails in tests.
